scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Ice melting review 3
experiments.focus: Review that a solid can change into a liquid without becoming a different substance.
student_observations: The ice becomes smaller over time.
Liquid water forms around the ice.
This is a physical change.
experiments.teacher_note: Use as a quick recap before moving to freezing.

experiments.title: Water freezing review 2
experiments.focus: Review that cooling can turn liquid water back into solid ice.
student_observations: Liquid water can return to a solid state.
Temperature matters in state changes.
The substance can stay the same while the state changes.
experiments.teacher_note: Pairs well with the melting review.

experiments.title: Water evaporation review 2
experiments.focus: Show that liquid water can slowly leave the container as vapor in a model situation.
student_observations: The water level can go down.
No new substance has to be added.
Heat and airflow can affect the speed.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect with drying clothes or puddles.

experiments.title: Sand and water filtration concept
experiments.focus: Show that some solids can be separated from water by using a simple filtration idea.
student_observations: The mixture can look cloudy at first.
Solid particles can be seen separately.
Some mixtures need separation rather than dissolution.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it conceptual and link it to filtration vocabulary.

experiments.title: Oil and water separation review
experiments.focus: Show that some liquids do not mix evenly and can form layers.
student_observations: The liquids can separate into layers.
Not every liquid mixes with water.
Density and miscibility are useful ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: A simple introduction to immiscible liquids.

experiments.title: Soap and water surface tension review 3
experiments.focus: Show that a small amount of soap can change how water behaves at the surface.
student_observations: Bubbles may form more easily.
The surface behaves differently.
Physical properties can change without a new substance being created.
experiments.teacher_note: Good as a short demo about everyday materials.

experiments.title: Sugar vs salt dissolving review 3
experiments.focus: Compare how two familiar solids behave in water.
student_observations: Both solids can dissolve in water in the model.
Different substances can dissolve differently.
Clear solutions are not all identical.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for a comparison table.

experiments.title: Flour in water cloudiness 3
experiments.focus: Show that some powders create cloudy mixtures instead of clear solutions.
student_observations: The liquid can look cloudy.
The powder does not disappear completely.
Mixtures can have different textures.
experiments.teacher_note: A simple comparison with sugar dissolving.

experiments.title: Glycerol viscosity review
experiments.focus: Show how some liquids flow more slowly than others.
student_observations: The liquid can seem thicker.
Flow speed can differ between liquids.
Viscosity is a useful physical property.
experiments.teacher_note: Good for introducing viscosity in simple language.

experiments.title: Chalk in water suspension review
experiments.focus: Show that some solids stay visible in water instead of forming a clear solution.
student_observations: The water can become cloudy.
Solid particles may stay visible.
Not every powder dissolves well.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this to compare with a true solution.

experiments.title: Vinegar and bicarbonate bubbles 3
experiments.focus: Introduce a safe classroom acid-carbonate concept with visible gas formation in the model.
student_observations: Bubbles can appear in the model.
Gas may be produced.
This is a useful reaction concept.
experiments.teacher_note: Use the reaction registry for the underlying logic.

experiments.title: Evaporation and residue review
experiments.focus: Show that removing water can leave a solid behind from a solution.
student_observations: The liquid part can decrease.
A solid residue can remain.
Evaporation can separate some mixtures.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect with drying and salt crystals.

experiments.title: Crystallization review 3
experiments.focus: Review how a dissolved substance can reappear when the solvent is removed.
student_observations: A clear solution can return to a solid form.
Crystals can form from the same substance.
Evaporation and crystallization are linked ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful after solutions and separation lessons.

experiments.title: Precipitation concept review 2
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that mixing two clear solutions can form a new solid in the model.
student_observations: A new solid can appear in the model.
Not all mixtures stay clear.
Some reactions can produce a precipitate.
experiments.teacher_note: Tie this directly to the validated registry.

experiments.title: Solution vs suspension compare 2
experiments.focus: Compare a clear solution with cloudy mixtures and visible particles.
student_observations: Some materials make clear solutions.
Some materials stay visible.
Mixture type depends on the particles and the solvent.
experiments.teacher_note: A good summary activity for revision.

experiments.title: Dissolution rate review
experiments.focus: Compare how quickly different solids dissolve in the classroom model.
student_observations: Different solids can dissolve at different speeds.
Stirring can change the result.
Solubility and rate are related but not identical ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for a discussion about rate vs amount.

experiments.title: Mixture classification review 2
experiments.focus: Group common classroom materials by solution, suspension or immiscible liquid examples.
student_observations: Some mixtures stay clear.
Some mixtures remain cloudy or separate.
Classification depends on how the materials behave together.
experiments.teacher_note: This is a broad summary activity for the whole unit.

experiments.title: Evaporation separation review 2
experiments.focus: Review how removing water can help separate a dissolved solid from a solution.
student_observations: Liquid can be removed while the solid remains.
Separation methods depend on the mixture type.
Evaporation and crystallization are connected ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: A useful end-of-unit recap.

experiments.title: Viscosity and flow review
experiments.focus: Compare how quickly different liquids flow and mix.
student_observations: Some liquids flow more slowly than others.
Viscosity changes how a liquid behaves.
Physical properties help identify materials.
experiments.teacher_note: Use as a revision bridge between liquids and mixtures.

experiments.title: Reversible change review
experiments.focus: Review which classroom changes are reversible and which are just physical state changes.
student_observations: Ice can melt and water can freeze again.
A dissolved solid can sometimes be recovered.
Reversible changes are useful in the model.
experiments.teacher_note: Good final revision activity before assessment.
